evals.name: physics-derivation-quiz
evals.prompt: Quiz me on special relativity — specifically time dilation and length contraction. I want the equations and derivations shown, PhD qualifying-exam level.
evals.expected_output: An interactive HTML quiz. Skill should ask/confirm difficulty (PhD/Research) before generating, then produce MathJax-rendered questions with derivations and real citations.

assertions.text: Asked the user to choose a difficulty level before generating the quiz
Output is a single self-contained .html file that opens as an interactive quiz
Equations are present and use LaTeX/MathJax delimiters, not plain text
At least one question includes a step-by-step derivation
Every explanation carries at least one specific, real citation (named source or URL/DOI), none fabricated
Difficulty is reflected in the content depth (graduate/PhD level, not beginner)

evals.name: general-topic-quiz
evals.prompt: Make me a 10-question practice quiz on the French Revolution to test myself before a class.
evals.expected_output: Skill asks difficulty (and confirms count ~10), then an interactive HTML quiz with clear explanations and citations to reputable history sources. Math/derivation optional here.

assertions.text: Asked for difficulty level before generating
Output is an interactive self-contained HTML quiz with feedback and scoring
Explanations are simplified and clear, each with a real citation
Multiple-choice distractors are plausible, not throwaway

evals.name: casual-stated-difficulty
evals.prompt: quiz me on how neural network backprop works, keep it fairly beginner friendly
evals.expected_output: User already implied difficulty (Foundational). Skill should map/confirm rather than re-ask from scratch, then build an interactive HTML quiz with intuitive explanations and citations, minimal heavy derivation.

assertions.text: Recognized the stated difficulty (beginner/Foundational) and confirmed rather than ignoring it
Output is an interactive self-contained HTML quiz
Explanations use plain language appropriate to a beginner
Equations, if any, render via MathJax rather than raw LaTeX text
